// This file does not compile, on purpose. It is lesson 10, THE THIRD WALL,
// in docs/teaching-generics.md.
//
// Go 1.27 lifted the restriction lesson 5 relies on -- a generic method on a
// CONCRETE type is legal there (see wall_method_type_param.go, and note this
// file is built at -lang=go1.27, not go1.21, precisely because 1.27 is where
// that distinction becomes visible: at go1.21 both files fail the same way,
// which would hide the point). What is attempted here is different and
// fails for a different, narrower reason: a type parameter on a method
// declared inside an INTERFACE, rather than on a concrete type's method.
// That one Go still rejects, at 1.27 and, as far as the language spec goes,
// indefinitely -- it is not gated behind a language version the way lesson
// 5's restriction was.
//
// It has a .go.txt extension, not .go: go/parser (what gofmt uses) rejects a
// type-parameter list on an interface method as a syntax error, not just a
// type-check error the way cmd/compile does for the concrete-method case in
// wall_method_type_param.go -- so as a plain .go file it would make
// `gofmt -l .` fail on this repository even though it is deliberately never
// built by `go build ./...` (a bare .go file WOULD be, since go/build's
// testdata skip only excludes it from package pattern discovery like ./...,
// not from an explicit file argument or gofmt's directory walk).
//
// fpgen/wall_test.go's TestWallInterfaceMethodTypeParams copies this file's
// text into a temporary .go file and runs
// `go build -gcflags=-lang=go1.27` on that copy, so lesson 10's closing
// argument rests on a checked fact rather than a claim that could go stale
// the way lesson 5's did.
package testdata

type List[A any] struct {
	Head A
	Tail *List[A]
}

type Mapper[A any] interface {
	Map[B any](f func(A) B) *List[B]
}
